findings.issue: These replacements for 'no text we hold' turn a gap in the project's library into a claim about the whole of scholarship. A reader takes 'no direct tie has been traced' as 'historians have not traced it'. That is false. Historians have long traced the awakening's ties to later American revivals, and to Black conversion: Samuel Davies's Hanover work, which this same field names, is a standard case. It is also more than the method's 'qualify with the reason' allows: the honest reason is uncertainty about how direct the tie was, not that nobody has traced it. B9's 'that line has not been traced' has the same fault. Continuity from the 18th-century Welsh revival to 1904-05 is widely discussed, and the 1904 entry argues for independent beginnings. Both are new problems, and the round-1 fix brought them in.

fix.B0_last_two_sentences: Later American revivals and the Black Church may owe it a debt too. How direct that debt was is hard to say.
fix.B0_whole_field: The awakening grew out of New England's Puritan churches. Jonathan Edwards built on their books. George Whitefield, the English Methodist preacher, made it normal to preach from town to town. It also reached the middle and southern colonies, through preachers like the Tennents and the revival at Hanover, Virginia. Historians do not agree whether that was the same movement or another one. William Carey, who began the Baptist mission to India, held up its missionary David Brainerd as a model. Later American revivals and the Black Church may owe it a debt too. How direct that debt was is hard to say.
fix.B9_last_sentence: Its hymns and habits of revival may lie behind the Welsh revival of 1904-05, but how far is hard to say.
fix.B9_whole_field: A sister movement to English Methodism. It began at the same time, kept in touch with its leaders, and ran in its own language. Its hymns and habits of revival may lie behind the Welsh revival of 1904-05, but how far is hard to say.
fix.note: 'Hard to say' states the uncertainty and makes no claim about what scholars have or have not done. If 'still argued' is preferred, it is also true for both: Butler's 1982 'interpretative fiction' thesis for B0, and the 1904 entry's own stress on independent beginnings for B9. It scores 60.8/7.9 and 76.2/6.2.
